title: Manual of Mineralogy
author: Cornelis Klein and Barbara Dutrow (originally by James D. Dana)
publication_date: Originally 1848 (Dana); latest editions updated periodically, with Klein & Dutrow's 23rd edition published in 2007
target_audience: Undergraduate and graduate students of geology and mineralogy
core_themes: Physical and chemical properties of minerals
primary_purpose: To provide a comprehensive and authoritative reference on the principles, methods, and classification of minerals for use in academic study, teaching, and professional practice.

structure_format.narrative_style: Formal and pedagogical; precise scientific language with explanatory illustrations and tables
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic sections: basic concepts, crystallography, mineral properties, systematic mineralogy by mineral class, and identification guides
features: Tables and charts for mineral identification

key_concepts_lessons: Minerals are classified based on chemical composition and crystal structure.
Understanding crystallography is key to identifying and differentiating minerals.
Physical properties such as hardness, luster, color, and cleavage aid in field and lab identification.
Chemical analysis and optical mineralogy provide definitive identification in scientific settings.
Knowledge of mineral genesis and stability helps interpret geologic processes and Earth's history.
notable_features: Standard reference for mineralogy curricula globally
Traces its roots to James D. Dana's renowned 19th-century work
Comprehensive tables and field identification tools
Emphasizes both descriptive and practical (laboratory/field) aspects
cultural_historical_context: First published in the 19th century by James D. Dana, the Manual of Mineralogy has evolved with advances in mineralogical science and pedagogy. The work has remained a standard for generations, reflecting the centrality of mineralogy in earth sciences, petrology, and related fields.
reception_impact: Widely regarded as the authoritative introductory mineralogy textbook in English-speaking academia
Required reading in geology and mineralogy programs
Praised for clarity, depth, and comprehensive coverage
Updated regularly to reflect advances in mineralogical methods and classification
comparable_titles: Introduction to Mineralogy by William D. Nesse
Minerals: Their Constitution and Origin by Hans-Rudolf Wenk and Andrei Bulakh
Dana’s New Mineralogy, edited by R.V. Gaines, H.C.W. Skinner, E.E. Foord, B. Mason, A.J. Rosenzweig
